title: Fifth School, its teachers and vocal music lessons
summary: He describes Fifth School, principal A.P. Williams, teachers Mrs. Lewis and others, and singing lessons; he left at fifteen for Southern University.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah, tell me about the school.

I left fifth school at the County Franklin and Padilla, fifteen years of age. I left there to go to what you call Southern University. I'd be on Southern University Magazine. You know what I said about that? It's down in Baton Rouge. But it was then on Southern University Magazine.
Well, what was the school at the... Fredino and Franklin? Who had that school?

It was called Fifth School. It was controlled by a man by the name of Arthur P. Williams. He was the principal. He called his name Arthur Principal Williams. A.P. Williams we called him. And did he have any other teachers?
Who were some of the teachers? Oh, yes.

I had quite a few teachers. I had some of the names of the teachers. The later teachers was Mrs. Lewis. She came around on Fridays. Taught music, vocal music. Mrs. Lewis. And we had Mr. Vega. That's the name of some of the teachers. Mrs. Vega. And Ms. Emma Rose Williams. That's the name of some of the teachers. Emma Rose Williams.
What did Ms. Lewis teach you? Ms. Lewis, she taught music. Yeah, but I mean what did she teach you personally? Did she teach you music in general? No. Or one particular instrument?
Not to play music, but she taught me vocal music. I was in the class that she's teaching in. Come around and teach all the pupils in the class like that.
That's it. Oh, you'd all sing it once or one at a time?
